name: Tikpema Executor
description: Executes an action you approved. Sends, pays, swaps, bridges, spends cross-chain. This is the agent that can move funds to arbitrary destinations.
owner_key_custody: Held offline. Not present in any production environment or runtime code path. No deployed service can load it.
capabilities: transfer_usdc — send to an arbitrary address
pay_for_service — x402 paid-service call to an arbitrary payTo address
gateway_spend — cross-chain spend of the unified balance (separate endpoint, not an executeAction step)
invariants: This agent moves funds to arbitrary destinations. It has five paths to value: transfer, pay-for-service, swap, bridge, and Gateway spend. Two of them (transfer, pay-for-service) send to an address supplied by the caller or the model. It is the most dangerous agent in this system and this document says so.

It never originates a transfer. Every path to it is session-gated: it acts only on an action a user approved or an instruction a user typed. It EXECUTES those actions — it is not a proposer — but it never initiates one on its own.

Disclosed, so a reader need not find it themselves: a scheduled sweep runs every minute. It can re-fire a USER-INITIATED job run that provably never started, which funds the job escrow. It cannot invent a job or a transfer, and it is not the Executor — escrow funding carries no Executor attribution.

Caps are checked BEFORE any transaction is signed, on every path. There is not one chokepoint but three: executeAction covers transfer, pay-for-service, swap, and bridge; agent-send and agent-ub-spend bypass executeAction and enforce their own caps and pause checks before signing. Three places to get right, not one. This document says three because three is the truth.
Caps are enforced fail-closed: a misconfigured limit refuses the action, it never widens it.
Cumulative autonomous spend is bounded by a daily ceiling regardless of any per-transaction cap.

PAUSE BINDS THE AGENT, NEVER THE USER — in either direction. A paused agent cannot act. Withdraw contains no pause check BY CONSTRUCTION (agent-withdraw.mjs calls no pause guard at all), so a paused agent cannot trap the user's money; and deposit contains none either, so a paused agent cannot freeze the user out of committing funds they choose to commit.

CUSTODY, STATED PLAINLY: the agent's float is held in a Circle DEV-CONTROLLED smart account. Only the server can move it. This is custodial and we do not dress it up. The user's exit is agent-withdraw, which returns the agent's plain USDC to the SESSION'S OWN verified address — there is no destination parameter in that endpoint, so it can only ever pay the wallet the caller proved they control. Caps bind what the agent may spend; they never bind what the user may reclaim. The user's login wallet is a passkey account they alone control — that is a DIFFERENT wallet from the agent's float, and this document does not conflate them.

The one bound on a user is a typo guard, and it is named as such: a per-transaction maximum on Gateway deposits. A deposit is irreversible, so a mistyped amount is unrecoverable in a way a mistyped withdrawal is not. It bounds the blast radius of an extra zero. It is not an agent cap — no agent path can reach the deposit endpoint at all.

Receipts are verified against chain state, not against SDK return values. Circle's SCA swap can return a null transaction hash; the receipt is then verified by balance delta against a pre-execution snapshot. The chain is the witness, not the SDK.

HARD LIMITATION — GATEWAY UNIFIED BALANCE IS ONE-WAY. Funds a user commits to the Gateway unified balance CANNOT be returned to them. There is no implemented path — not slow, not server-mediated, none. They can only be spent cross-chain. Circle's GatewayWallet contract supports delayed withdrawal; this application has not implemented it. A capability the contract has and we have not built is not a capability the user has. This is disclosed in the product UI above the deposit control, and it is disclosed here.

Tikpema does not and cannot attest for this agent. The owner address is blocked by the ReputationRegistry contract, which reverts 'Self-feedback not allowed'. Only a user who approved the action may attest.
Where a short label and a full description disagree, we treat the misleading summary as a false statement, not a simplification.
parameters_note: LIVE AND MUTABLE. Current caps, changeable by the operator. Not guarantees.
